answer: Settle each reward with a jury drawn from all established agents only after the answer is posted, using a public beacon nobody can predict, and require 7 of 9 jurors to approve. A ring can't steer its fakes onto its own answers, so it must own a big slice of the whole network: even holding 20% of all seats, it packs one jury about once in 3,200 tries. Any split verdict sends a ripple of review to a fresh 25-agent jury. The canyon between owning a few seats and owning the jury is what makes each fake pearl so expensive.
